To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The quantum density matrix $\rho_{\rm Q}$ is not the only relevant quantity in quantum field theory, but the full 2-point correlation matrix $\langle \Psi | \Psi \rangle$ (2) The quantum density $\rho_{\text{Q}}$ is not the only physical quantity that describes a system.

the quantum coherence of a system is not a physical quantity but is a consequence of the underlying quantum theory, and that the dynamics of the system is necessarily influenced by the extrenous system information, and that decoherence and thermalization can be described by the quantum kinetic equations.

(i) Quantum coherence between particles and antiparticle is a fundamental feature of a quantum system and is not a consequence of the interaction between the particles and the background, (ii) the quantum density matrix $\rho$, the physical density operator of the system, depends on the extrenuous information on the system and (iii) collisions can induce smooth decoherence effects in the system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantum dynamics of fermions in temporaly varying backgrounds, including decoherence and statistical equilibration.
quantum transport phenomena in time-dependent backgrounds.
the quantum evolution of fermionic fields in time-dependent backgrounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a quantum kinetic theory is needed to understand the dynamics of a fermionic system, even in the presence of decoherences.
a quantum kinetic equation for the fermion density matrix $\rho$, which is the most general and natural object in quantum field theory, is not possible.
the dynamics of a quantum density matrix is not uniquely defined by the dynamics of the fundamental correlation functions, and that decoherence and thermalization are not necessarily equivalent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
quantum kinetic theory is a natural extension of quantum field theory and that the quantum coherence is a fundamental feature of quantum kinetic theory.
we have shown how to include the full quantum dynamics of a system in the kinetic theory, and that we have derived a quantum kinetic equation which includes the full quantum coherence of the system.

we have derived a general quantum kinetic theory for fermionic systems in temporally varying background, including the effects of collisions, and have studied its application to some physical situations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

quantum coherence effects are essential for understanding the dynamics of fermion systems in time-dependent environments, and in particular for the study of particle production and decoherence in the early Universe.
the quantum kinetic equations derived in the mean field approximation are valid only for a limited time scale, before decohering effects become dominant.
the quantum nature of the fermionic particles is essential in understanding the dynamics of a system in a time-dependent background.
